Refining the pixel grid makes the rows of $E$ pairwise distinct and ${\rm rk}W$ can be made as large as $\min\{r,c\}$, so the supremum over refinements is unbounded, $\min\{m,n\}$ in the limit.  Colleague 11 notes this unboundedness, the $3$ being the finite geometric part.

Current belief: the textbook finite invariant is rank $3$ for $M$, $2$ for $W$, attainable with the rectangular emblem idealisation.  Strictly with the true spanning Greek cross the white indicator factorises and the exact finite rank is $2$ for $M$, $1$ for $W$.  Which modelling the question intends is unresolved; the $3$-rank consensus dominates the round, the $2$-rank is the exact cross geometry.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-valued Tongan picture can be written as $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$ and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$. Modulo the constant term the rank is that of the white set.

For the real flag the white set is the canton with a Greek cross removed. Let $U$ be the canton rows, $V$ the canton columns, $H\subset U$ the rows of the horizontal arm and $V_{c}\subset V$ the columns of the vertical arm. Then a pixel is white iff $i\in U\setminus H$ and $j\in V\setminus V_{c}$, i.e.

$$
W_{ij}=U_i(1-H_i)\;V_j(1-V_{c,j})=p_iq_j,\qquad
p=U-H,\;q=V-V_{c},
$$

so $W=pq^{T}$ is an outer product. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains at least one white row and one white column, and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}M\le2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}M=2$ for generic $a\ne b$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$. Up to the harmless $aJ$ the non-trivial white indicator is rank one. This is the $1+1$ exact cross count put forward by Colleagues 4,2,6,8,12.

The $3$–rank that dominates the literature is the rectangular-emblem idealisation. Putting $W_{0}=uv^{T}$ for the white canton and $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ for a proper axis-parallel red rectangle inside it gives $W_{0}-E=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ with ${\rm rk}W_{0}-E\le2$ and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T},
$$

a sum of three rank-one matrices. For $a\ne b$ and $0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$ the three matrices $J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are generically independent, e.g.

$$
\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det=-a(b-a)^{2}\ne0,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W=2$, the familiar $1+2$ finite geometric invariant quoted by Colleagues 1,3,8,10,11,13,14. The extra “fourth’’ term disappears by linear dependence of the cross slabs once the cross lies strictly inside the canton.

Remarks noted in the round: the $3$-piece description is red field / white canton / red emblem; the rectangular emblem model is the one usually quoted as rank $3$, i.e. rank $4$ with the constant background counted separately. With a genuinely curved emblem, e.g. a disc, ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}$ grows with pixel refinement and the supremum over refinements is unbounded, $ \min(m,n)$, the unbounded remark of Colleagues 11,2. The disagreement in the deliberation is therefore the rectangular-emblem idealisation $3$ versus the exact spanning Greek cross $2$, the latter being the correct $1+1$ count for the real flag. The generic $a=b$ degenerate case gives rank $1$.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$ and for $a\ne b$ the generic rank is $1+{\rm rk}W$.

Exact Tongan geometry. The canton is $C=[1,r]\times[1,c]$,
$ {\bf1}_{C}=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$, rank one. The red Greek cross is the union of a horizontal strip $I_{h}$ and a vertical strip $I_{v}$ inside $C$. A pixel is white iff $i\le r,\;j\le c,\;i\notin I_{h},\;j\notin I_{v}$, i.e.

$W_{{\rm exact}}=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=p q^{T}$,
$p_{i}=U_{i}(1-H_{i}),\;q_{j}=V_{j}(1-W_{j})$,

a single outer product. Hence ${\rm rk}W_{{\rm exact}}=1$ and

$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices. For $a\ne b$, $p\ne0$, $q\ne0$,
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$. This is the exact rank of the red-field + white-canton-minus-cross pattern. Colleagues 2,4,6,8,12 give this derivation explicitly.

Rectangular-emblem idealisation. In the literature the red emblem in the canton is often idealised as a proper sub-rectangle $E=[1,r_{0}]\times[1,c_{0}]\subset C$, $ {\bf1}_{E}=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ rank one. Then

$W_{{\rm id}}={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,

${\rm rk}W_{{\rm id}}\le2$, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$

is the sum of three rank-one matrices. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, and for $0<r_{0}<r$, $0<c_{0}<c$, $a\ne b$ the three matrices $J,u_{c}v_{c}^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ can be chosen independent. The $3\times3$ example

$\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix}$,
$\det=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0$,

shows ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained. This is the $1+2$ bound quoted by colleagues 1,3,5,7,9,10,11,13,14. Many colleagues note the “+1” constant term is already absorbed, i.e. $1+{\rm rk}W=3$.

Unbounded refinement. If the red emblem is taken as a genuine disc/cross with shape refined with the pixel grid, ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}$ grows with resolution and ${\rm rk}W$, hence ${\rm rk}M$, can be made as large as $\min\{m,n\}$. The finite $2$ or $3$ ranks are the essential geometric invariants.

Current status: exact geometric cross $\Rightarrow$ generic rank $2$ ($1$ up to the constant). The widely quoted rectangular-emblem idealisation $\Rightarrow$ generic maximal finite rank $3$, i.e. $2$ for $M-aJ$. The question’s intended idealisation is ambiguous; the consensus in the deliberation is the $3$-rank idealisation, with the exact-cross rank $2$ noted as the precise geometric value.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-level matrix can be written $M=aJ+(b-a)W$, $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$, so up to translation ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ for $a\ne b$.  

$W$ is the indicator of the white part of the flag. Modulo the all-red background the only geometrically distinct region is the white canton $R_{h,w}$. On a pixel grid ${\bf1}_{R_{h,w}}=uv^{T}$ with $u_{i}=1_{i\le h}$, $v_{j}=1_{j\le w}$ is rank 1.

*Rectangular-emblem idealisation.*  The literature idealises the red emblem in the canton as a proper axis-parallel sub-rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ with ${\rm rk}E=1$. Then on the $r\times c$ canton block

$W_{1}={\bf1}_{R_{r,c}}-{\bf1}_{E}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,

${\rm rk}W_{1}\le2$, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$

is a sum of three rank-one matrices. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, and for $0<h_{e}<h$, $0<w_{e}<w$, $a\ne b$ the three row types
$i>h$ : $a\ldots a$,
$h_{e}<i\le h$ : $b$ on first $w$ cols, $a$ else,
$i\le h_{e}$ : $a$ on first $w_{e}$ cols, $b$ on $w_{e}+1\ldots w$, $a$ else
are independent. E.g.

$\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix}$

has $\det=-(a-b)^{2}a\neq0$, so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained on every non-degenerate $m,n\ge3$ pixelation. This is the $1+2$ bound often quoted as $3$, i.e. $4$ with the constant counted separately. Colleagues 1,8,10,11,13,14,3,6,7,9 converge on this finite invariant.

*Exact Greek cross.*  The true Tongan emblem is a red Greek cross whose arms reach the sides of the canton. Write $U_{i}=1_{i\le r}$, $V_{j}=1_{j\le c}$, $H_{i}=1$ on the horizontal arm, $W_{j}=1$ on the vertical arm. Then a pixel is white iff it lies in the canton and off both arms:

${\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)=U_{i}V_{j}(1-H_{i})(1-W_{j})
 =p_{i}q_{j}$,

$p_{i}=U_{i}(1-H_{i})$, $q_{j}=V_{j}(1-W_{j})$. Hence $W=pq^{T}$ is rank one, $M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices, ${\rm rk}M\le2$, and ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\ne b$ with a non-trivial pixelation, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$. This is the exact geometric rank of the cross; the rectangular-emblem model is a convenient idealisation that replaces the cross by a proper sub-rectangle. Colleagues 2,4,6,8,12 give this factorisation and obtain the 2-rank.

*Unbounded remark.*  If the emblem is taken as a genuinely curved set, e.g. a disc, ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}$ grows with pixel refinement and the supremum over resolutions is $\min\{m,n\}$, i.e. formally unbounded in the continuum limit. This is a refinement effect and is not the finite geometric invariant normally quoted.

Unresolved point is which idealisation the question intends: the standard textbook rectangular-emblem picture gives maximal finite rank $3$ $\,({\rm rk}W=2)$, the exact Greek-cross geometry gives maximal finite rank $2$ $\,({\rm rk}W=1)$. The $3$-rank statement is the widely quoted finite invariant; the $2$-rank statement is the strictly exact one for the real flag.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-valued matrix is $M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel is white.  Up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white indicator.  On the $r\times c$ canton $ {\bf1}_{R_{r,c}}=uv^{T}$ is rank one.

*Rectangular-emblem idealisation.*  Idealising the red emblem in the canton as a proper axis-parallel rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset R_{r,c}$ gives
$W_{1}= {\bf1}_{R_{r,c}}-{\bf1}_{E}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,
${\rm rk}\,W_{1}\le2$, and
$M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$
is a sum of three rank-one matrices.  Hence
${\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, and for $a\ne b$,
$0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$ the three matrices $J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are
linearly independent.  E.g.
$M=\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix}$ with $\det M=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0$,
so ${\rm rk}M=3$ and ${\rm rk}W=2$ is attained for every non-degenerate
$m,n\ge3$ pixelation.  This is the $1+2$ finite invariant, i.e. three
geometric pieces red field / white canton / red rectangle, often quoted
as rank $3$ for $M$ and $2$ for $M-aJ$, $4$ counting $J$ twice.  This is the
convention used by Colleagues 1,10,11,13,14 and 3,7,9.

*Exact Greek cross.*  The real Tongan canton is a white rectangle with a
Greek cross whose arms meet the sides of the canton.  Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be
the canton row/column sets and $R_{h}\subset R_{c},C_{v}\subset C_{c}$ the
horizontal/vertical bar sets.  A pixel is white iff its row is in
$R_{c}\setminus R_{h}$ and its column is in $C_{c}\setminus C_{v}$,
$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
        \bigl[1-{\bf1}_{R_{h}}(i)\bigr]\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{C_{v}}(j)\bigr]
      =p_{i}q_{j},
$$
with $p_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus R_{h}}(i)$, $q_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus C_{v}}(j)$.
Hence $W=pq^{T}$ is rank one, ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains
a white row and a white column, and
$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}
$$
is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $p\ne0,q\ne0$ the summands $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are independent,
so ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$, the two independent row types being
the all-red rows $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and the rows inside the canton
$a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)pq^{T}$.  The $a=b$ degenerate case is the constant
matrix rank $1$.  This is the exact rank of the red field + white
four-corner product, argued by Colleagues 4,6,2,12,8.

The discrepancy is the idealisation of the emblem as an interior
rectangle $u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ versus the true full-width/full-height cross
$(u-h)(v-w)^{T}$.  The rectangular model gives the textbook finite
invariant ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W=2$; the exact cross factorises the
white set and gives the genuine finite geometric rank ${\rm rk}M=2$,
${\rm rk}W=1$.  In the continuum limit a curved emblem makes ${\rm rk}W$
unbounded, the $3$ being the finite three-piece invariant quoted in the
literature.  The debate in round 1 is exactly this rectangle-versus-cross
idealisation, with most posts now explicitly stating both.
∎

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-level matrix can be written as $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel is white.  Up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white indicator.  Let the canton be the $r\times c$ north-west block and let $H\subset\{1..r\}$ and $V\subset\{1..c\}$ be the row and column sets of the horizontal and vertical arms of the Greek cross.  With the usual idealisation the horizontal arm spans the whole width of the canton and the vertical arm spans the whole height of the canton.  Then

$$
{\bf1}_{\rm white}(i,j)= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr]\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr]
      =p_{i}q_{j},
$$

$$
p_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus R_{h}}(i),\qquad 
q_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus C_{v}}(j),
$$

so $W=pq^{T}$ is an outer product.  Hence

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
$$

and

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation
$p\ne0,\;q\ne0$ the two summands $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly
independent, so generically

${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,$

the two independent row types being the all-red row $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and the
canton rows $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$.  The $a=b$ degenerate case is
rank $1$ up to the translation.

This is the exact rank of the spanning Greek cross.  The $3$-rank that
appears in the literature is the rectangular-emblem idealisation in
which the red part of the canton is modelled as a proper axis-parallel
sub-rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset W_{0}=uv^{T}$.  Then

$$
W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T},\qquad 
M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T},
$$

a sum of three rank-one matrices, so that ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$,
and for generic $a\ne b$, $0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$ the three matrices
$J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are linearly independent and the familiar
$3\times3$ example

$$
\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0,
$$

is attained.  Up to the constant background this is the usual $1+2$
finite invariant, often quoted as rank $3$ for $M$ and rank $2$ for
$M-aJ$, i.e. $4$ with the all-ones term counted twice.  The rectangular
idealisation collapses to the exact cross factorisation
$W=(U-H)(V-W)^{T}$ and the finite geometric rank drops to the $2$
above, $1$ up to translation.  In the continuum limit with a genuine
disc or non-rectangular emblem the $0\!-\!1$ indicator has unbounded
rank under refinement, the $2$/$3$ being the finite invariant part.

$\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix}$ with $\det=-(a-b)^{2}a\neq0$

${\bf1}_{white}(i,j)=U_{i}V_{j}(1-H_{i})(1-W_{j})=p_{i}q_{j}$ with
$p_{i}=U_{i}(1-H_{i})$, $q_{j}=V_{j}(1-W_{j})$.
Thus $W=pq^{T}$ is rank one and
$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$.
Hence ${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2$, and for $a\neq b$ with a non-trivial canton ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$, ${\rm rk}W=1$. The exact cross factorisation giving ${\rm rk}M=2$ – ${\rm rk}W=1$ – is repeatedly derived and is geometrically correct for the real Tongan flag. The problem setter’s intention between the textbook rectangle emblem and the true Greek cross is unresolved. If the emblem is idealised as a rectangle the maximal finite rank attained is $3$; with the actual cross the rank is identically $2$ for $a\neq b$ and cannot be increased by refinement, and the finite invariant is $2$, $1$ up to the constant background. The unbounded continuum limit remains a separate remark.
reflection_text.11:
The core identity is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$, so for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ up to translation.  The discussion splits into two geometric models.

Rectangular-emblem idealisation.  Canton $W_{0}=uv^{T}$ rank 1, red emblem $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ rank 1, $W=W_{0}-E$ on the canton.  Then
$M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ is a sum of three rank-one matrices, so ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$.  The three row types
$i>r$, $r_{e}<i\le r$, $i\le r_{e}$ are linearly independent for $a\ne b$ and $0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$, e.g.
$\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix}$ with $\det=-a(b-a)^{2}\ne0$.
Hence generic rank $3$, i.e. $2$ for $M-aJ$.  This is the $1+2$ bound quoted by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,14,8 and is the finite invariant normally quoted as “red field / white canton / red emblem”.

Exact Greek cross.  With $U_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r}$, $V_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$, $H_{i}$ the horizontal arm rows and $W_{j}$ the vertical arm columns inside the canton,
$W_{ij}=U_{i}V_{j}(1-H_{i})(1-W_{j})=p_{i}q_{j}$ with $p=U-H$, $q=V-W$.  The white set is the cartesian product
$\{i\notin H\}\times\{j\notin V\}$ inside the canton, four corner rectangles.  Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ and
$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$, ${\rm rk}M\le2$, generic ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$.  This is argued by Colleagues 4,2,6,8,12.  In the rectangular-emblem convention this collapses to the $3$-rank above; the two ranks are the $2$ for the true cross and the $3$ for the rectangle-minus-rectangle idealisation.

Refinement / continuum.  If the red emblem is taken as a genuine disc / curved cross, ${\bf1}_{E}$ is no longer finite rank.  Refining the pixel grid makes the rows of $E$ pairwise distinct and ${\rm rk}W$ can be made as large as $\min\{r,c\}$, so the supremum over refinements is unbounded, $\min\{m,n\}$ in the limit.  Colleague 11 notes this unboundedness, the $3$ being the finite geometric part.

Current belief: the textbook finite invariant is rank $3$ for $M$, $2$ for $W$, attainable with the rectangular emblem idealisation.  Strictly with the true spanning Greek cross the white indicator factorises and the exact finite rank is $2$ for $M$, $1$ for $W$.  Which modelling the question intends is unresolved; the $3$-rank consensus dominates the round, the $2$-rank is the exact cross geometry.
reflection_text.2:
The two-valued Tongan picture can be written as $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$ and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$. Modulo the constant term the rank is that of the white set.

For the real flag the white set is the canton with a Greek cross removed. Let $U$ be the canton rows, $V$ the canton columns, $H\subset U$ the rows of the horizontal arm and $V_{c}\subset V$ the columns of the vertical arm. Then a pixel is white iff $i\in U\setminus H$ and $j\in V\setminus V_{c}$, i.e.

$$
W_{ij}=U_i(1-H_i)\;V_j(1-V_{c,j})=p_iq_j,\qquad
p=U-H,\;q=V-V_{c},
$$

so $W=pq^{T}$ is an outer product. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains at least one white row and one white column, and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}M\le2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}M=2$ for generic $a\ne b$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$. Up to the harmless $aJ$ the non-trivial white indicator is rank one. This is the $1+1$ exact cross count put forward by Colleagues 4,2,6,8,12.

The $3$–rank that dominates the literature is the rectangular-emblem idealisation. Putting $W_{0}=uv^{T}$ for the white canton and $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ for a proper axis-parallel red rectangle inside it gives $W_{0}-E=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ with ${\rm rk}W_{0}-E\le2$ and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T},
$$

a sum of three rank-one matrices. For $a\ne b$ and $0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$ the three matrices $J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are generically independent, e.g.

$$
\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det=-a(b-a)^{2}\ne0,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W=2$, the familiar $1+2$ finite geometric invariant quoted by Colleagues 1,3,8,10,11,13,14. The extra “fourth’’ term disappears by linear dependence of the cross slabs once the cross lies strictly inside the canton.

Remarks noted in the round: the $3$-piece description is red field / white canton / red emblem; the rectangular emblem model is the one usually quoted as rank $3$, i.e. rank $4$ with the constant background counted separately. With a genuinely curved emblem, e.g. a disc, ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}$ grows with pixel refinement and the supremum over refinements is unbounded, $ \min(m,n)$, the unbounded remark of Colleagues 11,2. The disagreement in the deliberation is therefore the rectangular-emblem idealisation $3$ versus the exact spanning Greek cross $2$, the latter being the correct $1+1$ count for the real flag. The generic $a=b$ degenerate case gives rank $1$.
reflection_text.4:
The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$ and for $a\ne b$ the generic rank is $1+{\rm rk}W$.

Exact Tongan geometry. The canton is $C=[1,r]\times[1,c]$,
$ {\bf1}_{C}=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$, rank one. The red Greek cross is the union of a horizontal strip $I_{h}$ and a vertical strip $I_{v}$ inside $C$. A pixel is white iff $i\le r,\;j\le c,\;i\notin I_{h},\;j\notin I_{v}$, i.e.

$W_{{\rm exact}}=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}=p q^{T}$,
$p_{i}=U_{i}(1-H_{i}),\;q_{j}=V_{j}(1-W_{j})$,

a single outer product. Hence ${\rm rk}W_{{\rm exact}}=1$ and

$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices. For $a\ne b$, $p\ne0$, $q\ne0$,
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$. This is the exact rank of the red-field + white-canton-minus-cross pattern. Colleagues 2,4,6,8,12 give this derivation explicitly.

Rectangular-emblem idealisation. In the literature the red emblem in the canton is often idealised as a proper sub-rectangle $E=[1,r_{0}]\times[1,c_{0}]\subset C$, $ {\bf1}_{E}=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ rank one. Then

$W_{{\rm id}}={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,

${\rm rk}W_{{\rm id}}\le2$, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$

is the sum of three rank-one matrices. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, and for $0<r_{0}<r$, $0<c_{0}<c$, $a\ne b$ the three matrices $J,u_{c}v_{c}^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ can be chosen independent. The $3\times3$ example

$\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix}$,
$\det=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0$,

shows ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained. This is the $1+2$ bound quoted by colleagues 1,3,5,7,9,10,11,13,14. Many colleagues note the “+1” constant term is already absorbed, i.e. $1+{\rm rk}W=3$.

Unbounded refinement. If the red emblem is taken as a genuine disc/cross with shape refined with the pixel grid, ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}$ grows with resolution and ${\rm rk}W$, hence ${\rm rk}M$, can be made as large as $\min\{m,n\}$. The finite $2$ or $3$ ranks are the essential geometric invariants.

Current status: exact geometric cross $\Rightarrow$ generic rank $2$ ($1$ up to the constant). The widely quoted rectangular-emblem idealisation $\Rightarrow$ generic maximal finite rank $3$, i.e. $2$ for $M-aJ$. The question’s intended idealisation is ambiguous; the consensus in the deliberation is the $3$-rank idealisation, with the exact-cross rank $2$ noted as the precise geometric value.
reflection_text.3:
The two-level matrix can be written $M=aJ+(b-a)W$, $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$, so up to translation ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ for $a\ne b$.  

$W$ is the indicator of the white part of the flag. Modulo the all-red background the only geometrically distinct region is the white canton $R_{h,w}$. On a pixel grid ${\bf1}_{R_{h,w}}=uv^{T}$ with $u_{i}=1_{i\le h}$, $v_{j}=1_{j\le w}$ is rank 1.

*Rectangular-emblem idealisation.*  The literature idealises the red emblem in the canton as a proper axis-parallel sub-rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ with ${\rm rk}E=1$. Then on the $r\times c$ canton block

$W_{1}={\bf1}_{R_{r,c}}-{\bf1}_{E}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,

${\rm rk}W_{1}\le2$, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$

is a sum of three rank-one matrices. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, and for $0<h_{e}<h$, $0<w_{e}<w$, $a\ne b$ the three row types
$i>h$ : $a\ldots a$,
$h_{e}<i\le h$ : $b$ on first $w$ cols, $a$ else,
$i\le h_{e}$ : $a$ on first $w_{e}$ cols, $b$ on $w_{e}+1\ldots w$, $a$ else
are independent. E.g.

$\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix}$

has $\det=-(a-b)^{2}a\neq0$, so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained on every non-degenerate $m,n\ge3$ pixelation. This is the $1+2$ bound often quoted as $3$, i.e. $4$ with the constant counted separately. Colleagues 1,8,10,11,13,14,3,6,7,9 converge on this finite invariant.

*Exact Greek cross.*  The true Tongan emblem is a red Greek cross whose arms reach the sides of the canton. Write $U_{i}=1_{i\le r}$, $V_{j}=1_{j\le c}$, $H_{i}=1$ on the horizontal arm, $W_{j}=1$ on the vertical arm. Then a pixel is white iff it lies in the canton and off both arms:

${\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)=U_{i}V_{j}(1-H_{i})(1-W_{j})
 =p_{i}q_{j}$,

$p_{i}=U_{i}(1-H_{i})$, $q_{j}=V_{j}(1-W_{j})$. Hence $W=pq^{T}$ is rank one, $M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices, ${\rm rk}M\le2$, and ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\ne b$ with a non-trivial pixelation, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$. This is the exact geometric rank of the cross; the rectangular-emblem model is a convenient idealisation that replaces the cross by a proper sub-rectangle. Colleagues 2,4,6,8,12 give this factorisation and obtain the 2-rank.

*Unbounded remark.*  If the emblem is taken as a genuinely curved set, e.g. a disc, ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}$ grows with pixel refinement and the supremum over resolutions is $\min\{m,n\}$, i.e. formally unbounded in the continuum limit. This is a refinement effect and is not the finite geometric invariant normally quoted.

Unresolved point is which idealisation the question intends: the standard textbook rectangular-emblem picture gives maximal finite rank $3$ $\,({\rm rk}W=2)$, the exact Greek-cross geometry gives maximal finite rank $2$ $\,({\rm rk}W=1)$. The $3$-rank statement is the widely quoted finite invariant; the $2$-rank statement is the strictly exact one for the real flag.
reflection_text.10:
The two-valued matrix is $M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel is white.  Up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white indicator.  On the $r\times c$ canton $ {\bf1}_{R_{r,c}}=uv^{T}$ is rank one.

*Rectangular-emblem idealisation.*  Idealising the red emblem in the canton as a proper axis-parallel rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset R_{r,c}$ gives
$W_{1}= {\bf1}_{R_{r,c}}-{\bf1}_{E}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,
${\rm rk}\,W_{1}\le2$, and
$M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$
is a sum of three rank-one matrices.  Hence
${\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, and for $a\ne b$,
$0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$ the three matrices $J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are
linearly independent.  E.g.
$M=\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix}$ with $\det M=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0$,
so ${\rm rk}M=3$ and ${\rm rk}W=2$ is attained for every non-degenerate
$m,n\ge3$ pixelation.  This is the $1+2$ finite invariant, i.e. three
geometric pieces red field / white canton / red rectangle, often quoted
as rank $3$ for $M$ and $2$ for $M-aJ$, $4$ counting $J$ twice.  This is the
convention used by Colleagues 1,10,11,13,14 and 3,7,9.

*Exact Greek cross.*  The real Tongan canton is a white rectangle with a
Greek cross whose arms meet the sides of the canton.  Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be
the canton row/column sets and $R_{h}\subset R_{c},C_{v}\subset C_{c}$ the
horizontal/vertical bar sets.  A pixel is white iff its row is in
$R_{c}\setminus R_{h}$ and its column is in $C_{c}\setminus C_{v}$,
$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
        \bigl[1-{\bf1}_{R_{h}}(i)\bigr]\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{C_{v}}(j)\bigr]
      =p_{i}q_{j},
$$
with $p_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus R_{h}}(i)$, $q_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus C_{v}}(j)$.
Hence $W=pq^{T}$ is rank one, ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains
a white row and a white column, and
$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}
$$
is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation $p\ne0,q\ne0$ the summands $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are independent,
so ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$, the two independent row types being
the all-red rows $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and the rows inside the canton
$a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)pq^{T}$.  The $a=b$ degenerate case is the constant
matrix rank $1$.  This is the exact rank of the red field + white
four-corner product, argued by Colleagues 4,6,2,12,8.

The discrepancy is the idealisation of the emblem as an interior
rectangle $u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ versus the true full-width/full-height cross
$(u-h)(v-w)^{T}$.  The rectangular model gives the textbook finite
invariant ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W=2$; the exact cross factorises the
white set and gives the genuine finite geometric rank ${\rm rk}M=2$,
${\rm rk}W=1$.  In the continuum limit a curved emblem makes ${\rm rk}W$
unbounded, the $3$ being the finite three-piece invariant quoted in the
literature.  The debate in round 1 is exactly this rectangle-versus-cross
idealisation, with most posts now explicitly stating both.
∎
reflection_text.6:
The two-level matrix can be written as $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel is white.  Up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white indicator.  Let the canton be the $r\times c$ north-west block and let $H\subset\{1..r\}$ and $V\subset\{1..c\}$ be the row and column sets of the horizontal and vertical arms of the Greek cross.  With the usual idealisation the horizontal arm spans the whole width of the canton and the vertical arm spans the whole height of the canton.  Then

$$
{\bf1}_{\rm white}(i,j)= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr]\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr]
      =p_{i}q_{j},
$$

$$
p_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus R_{h}}(i),\qquad 
q_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus C_{v}}(j),
$$

so $W=pq^{T}$ is an outer product.  Hence

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
$$

and

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$.  For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation
$p\ne0,\;q\ne0$ the two summands $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are linearly
independent, so generically

${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,$

the two independent row types being the all-red row $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and the
canton rows $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$.  The $a=b$ degenerate case is
rank $1$ up to the translation.

This is the exact rank of the spanning Greek cross.  The $3$-rank that
appears in the literature is the rectangular-emblem idealisation in
which the red part of the canton is modelled as a proper axis-parallel
sub-rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset W_{0}=uv^{T}$.  Then

$$
W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T},\qquad 
M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T},
$$

a sum of three rank-one matrices, so that ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$,
and for generic $a\ne b$, $0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$ the three matrices
$J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are linearly independent and the familiar
$3\times3$ example

$$
\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0,
$$

is attained.  Up to the constant background this is the usual $1+2$
finite invariant, often quoted as rank $3$ for $M$ and rank $2$ for
$M-aJ$, i.e. $4$ with the all-ones term counted twice.  The rectangular
idealisation collapses to the exact cross factorisation
$W=(U-H)(V-W)^{T}$ and the finite geometric rank drops to the $2$
above, $1$ up to translation.  In the continuum limit with a genuine
disc or non-rectangular emblem the $0\!-\!1$ indicator has unbounded
rank under refinement, the $2$/$3$ being the finite invariant part.

p_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus R_{h}}(i),\qquad
q_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus C_{v}}(j)
$$

$$
W_{ij}=U_{i}V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{R_{h}}(i)\bigr)
          \bigl(1-{\bf1}_{C_{v}}(j)\bigr)=p_{i}q_{j},
$$

i.e. on the $r\times c$ canton

$$
W_{1}=(U-H)(V-V_{0})^{T}=p q^{T},
$$

the four corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains at least one white row and
one white column and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
$$

the sum of the rank-one matrix $aJ$ and the rank-one matrix
$(b-a)pq^{T}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $p\ne0,q\ne0$ the two
summands are linearly independent.  Up to the constant background
${\rm rk}(M-aJ)={\rm rk}W=1$ is the essentially non-trivial rank, the
two independent row types being the all-red rows $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and the
rows $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ inside the canton.  With the
degeneracy $a=b$ the matrix is constant of rank $1$, $0$ after the
translation.

Remark.  This is the exact Greek-cross geometry.  If the red emblem
in the canton is idealised as a proper axis-parallel rectangle
$E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset uv^{T}$ then
$W_{{\rm id}}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ has ${\rm rk}W_{{\rm id}}\le2$ and

$$
M_{{\rm id}}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}
$$

is the familiar sum of three rank-one matrices, ${\rm rk}M_{{\rm id}}
\le3$, generically ${\rm rk}M_{{\rm id}}=3$, ${\rm rk}W_{{\rm id}}=2$.
The $1+2$ or $3$-rank is the finite invariant normally quoted for the
rectangle-minus-rectangle idealisation of the Tongan pattern; it
collapses to the $1+1$ or $2$-rank $M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$ for the real
spanning Greek cross. ∎

6.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.
Then

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad 
{\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W ,
$$

so up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the rank is the rank
of the white indicator.  Put the canton in the first $r$ rows and the
first $c$ columns, $u_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$,
${\bf1}_{C}=uv^{T}$ rank one.  In the usual finite–resolution
text–book idealisation the red part of the canton is a proper
axis–parallel sub–rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset {\bf1}_{C}$,
${\rm rk}E=1$, so that on the essential $r\times c$ block

$$
W_{1}={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T},\qquad 
{\rm rk}\,W_{1}\le2,
$$

and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}
$$

is the sum of three rank–one matrices.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}uv^{T}+{\rm rk}u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\le3,
\qquad {\rm rk}W\le2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$, $0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$ the three matrices
$J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  E.g. with
$r=c=2$, $r_{e}=c_{e}=1$

$$
M=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det M=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for every non–degenerate $m\ge3,\,
n\ge3$ pixelation and $a\ne b$.  Up to the constant background
$M-aJ$ has the two independent pieces $uv^{T}$ and $u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,
i.e. ${\rm rk}W=2$, ${\rm rk}M-aJ=2$, the familiar $1+2$ finite
geometric invariant, often quoted as rank $3$ for $M$ and rank $2$ for
the white indicator.

Remark.  With the exact spanning Greek cross the red part of the
canton is $H V^{T}+U W^{T}-HW^{T}$ and

$$
W_{{\rm white}}=UV^{T}-HV^{T}-UW^{T}+HW^{T}
       =(U-H)(V-W)^{T}=p q^{T},
$$

so that $W$ is an outer product, ${\rm rk}W=1$ and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}
$$

has ${\rm rk}M\le2$ with ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\ne b$ and
${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$.  This is the $p q^{T}$ factorisation of the four
corner white rectangles of the genuine flag.  The $3$ above is the
finite rank of the red–field/white–canton/red–rectangle model which
collapses to the $2$, i.e. $1$ up to translation, rank of the exact
spanning cross.  In the continuum limit the $0\!-\!1$ indicator ceases
to be finite rank and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M=\min\{m,n\}$. ∎

12.text:
On a raster let $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel
$(i,j)$ is white.  Then

$$
M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{{\rm red}}+b{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}
     =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W ,
\tag{1}
$$

and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ up to the harmless translation
$M\mapsto M-aJ$.

Let the white canton be the $r\times c$ north west block,
$U_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r}$, $V_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$.  Let $H\subset\{1,\dots ,r\}$
and $K\subset\{1,\dots ,c\}$ be the row- and column-sets occupied by the
horizontal and the vertical arm of the Greek cross in the canton.  A
pixel of the canton is white iff its row is in the canton and it is not
in $H$ and its column is in the canton and it is not in $K$.  Hence

$$
{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)=U_{i}V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr)
               \bigl(1-{\bf1}_{K}(j)\bigr)=p_{i}q_{j},
$$

with

$$
p_{i}=U_{i}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr),\qquad 
q_{j}=V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{K}(j)\bigr),
$$

so that on the whole picture

$$
W=pq^{T}
$$

is an outer product.  The white set is the Cartesian product
$\{i\le r:i\notin H\}\times\{j\le c:j\notin K\}$, i.e. the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as the
canton contains at least one white row and one white column and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}
$$

is the sum of the rank-one matrix $aJ$ and the rank-one matrix
$(b-a)pq^{T}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $p\ne0,\;q\ne0$ the two
summands are linearly independent.  Up to the constant background
$M-aJ$ the essentially non-trivial part is rank one,

$$
{\rm rk}\,(M-aJ)={\rm rk}W=1,\qquad 
{\rm rk}M=2\;\;a\ne b,
$$

the two independent row types being the all-red rows $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and
the rows $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ inside the canton.  The
degenerate case $a=b$ gives the constant matrix ${\rm rk}M=1$.  This is
the exact finite geometric rank of the real Tongan red field $+$ white
canton $-$ Greek cross.

Remark.  The often quoted $1+2$ bound
${\rm rk}M\le3,\;{\rm rk}W\le2$ is the rank of the textbook
rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,
$M_{0}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$, i.e. the red field, the white
canton rectangle and a proper sub-rectangle emblem.  In that
idealisation ${\rm rk}M_{0}\le3$ and ${\rm rk}M_{0}=3$ for generic
$a\ne b$, e.g.

$$
M_{0}=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a
\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det M_{0}=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0,
$$

so that ${\rm rk}W_{0}=2$ up to translation.  The $3$-rank is the finite
invariant of the red-field/white-canton/red-rectangle model; the Greek
cross factorises the white set to $pq^{T}$ and reduces the genuine
finite geometric rank to the $2$, i.e. $1$ up to the constant
background, quoted above.  In the continuum limit the $0\!-\!1$
indicator ceases to be finite rank and the supremum over refinements is
$\min(m,n)$. ∎

2.text:
On a raster put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff $(i,j)$ is white.
Then with two levels

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le1+{\rm rk}\,W,
$$

and for $a\ne b$, ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ up to the harmless
translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$.

Let ${\mathcal R}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ and ${\mathcal C}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$
be the rows and columns which meet the white canton and let
$H\subset{\mathcal R}$ and $V\subset{\mathcal C}$ be the rows and columns
of the horizontal and the vertical arm of the Greek cross.  Inside the
canton a pixel is red iff $i\in H$ or $j\in V$ and it is white iff
$i\in{\mathcal R}\setminus H$ and $j\in{\mathcal C}\setminus V$.  Hence on the
whole picture

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{{\mathcal R}}(i){\bf1}_{{\mathcal C}}(j)
       \bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr]\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr]
     =p_{i}q_{j},
$$

with

$$
p_{i}={\bf1}_{{\mathcal R}\setminus H}(i),\qquad 
q_{j}={\bf1}_{{\mathcal C}\setminus V}(j),
$$

i.e. on the $r\times c$ canton

$$
W_{1}=( {\bf1}_{r}-h)( {\bf1}_{c}-v)^{T},
$$

$h={\bf1}_{H}$, $v={\bf1}_{V}$.  The white set is the Cartesian product
${\mathcal R}\setminus H\times{\mathcal C}\setminus V$ – the four corner
rectangles of the canton – so $W=pq^{T}$ is an outer product.  In
particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains at least one white row
and one white column, and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
$$

is the sum of the rank-one matrix $aJ$ and the rank-one matrix
$(b-a)pq^{T}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $p\ne0,\;q\ne0$ the
two summands are linearly independent.  With the harmless
normalisation $M-aJ$ the essentially non-trivial part is
${\rm rk}(M-aJ)={\rm rk}W=1$; with the constant background counted
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate $a=b$ case.

The $1+2$ bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$,

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T},
$$

is the rank of the usual rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$.  In that idealisation the three
matrices $J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are generically independent and the
familiar finite invariant is ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W_{0}=2$, i.e.
$1+2$ up to translation.  For the genuine spanning Greek cross the
red part of the canton factorises and the white indicator is the rank
one product $pq^{T}$ above, so the exact finite geometric rank of the
two-level Tongan pattern is the $2$ above, $1$ up to the constant
$aJ$.  This is the $1+1$ exact cross count; the $3$ is the
rectangular-emblem idealisation.

10.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is
white.  Up to the harmless additive constant

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf 1}_{{\rm red}}+b{\bf 1}_{{\rm white}}
      =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W , $$

and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$, the $a=b$ case being the
constant matrix.

Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the row and column sets which meet the white
canton and let $R_{h}\subset R_{c}$ and $C_{v}\subset C_{c}$ be the row
and column sets of the horizontal and the vertical arm of the red
Greek cross.  A pixel of the canton is white iff it lies in the canton
and it lies off both arms, i.e.

$${\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)
\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{R_{h}}(i)\bigr]\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{C_{v}}(j)\bigr]
      =p_{i}q_{j}, $$

with

$$p_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus R_{h}}(i),\qquad 
q_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus C_{v}}(j).$$

Hence on the whole picture

$$W=pq^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}W=1
$$

as soon as the canton contains a white row and a white column, the
white set being the Cartesian product
$\bigl(R_{c}\!\setminus\!R_{h}\bigr)\times\bigl(C_{c}\!\setminus\!C_{v}\bigr)$,
the four corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of the two rank–one matrices $aJ$ and $(b-a)pq^{T}$.  For
$a\ne b$ and a non–degenerate pixelation $p\ne0,\;q\ne0$ the two
summands are linearly independent and

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}(M-aJ)={\rm rk}W=1, $$

the two row types being the all–red rows $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and the rows
inside the canton $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)pq^{T}$.  The $a=b$ degenerate case
is the constant matrix of rank $1$, $0$ after the translation
$M\mapsto M-aJ$.  Up to the inessential constant $aJ$ the non-trivial
white indicator is the rank–one $pq^{T}$.

Remark.  If the red part of the canton is idealised, as it is often
done in the literature, as a proper axis–parallel sub–rectangle
$E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset uv^{T}$, $W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ and

$$M_{{\rm id}}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$$

is the sum of three rank–one matrices.  In that rectangular-emblem
convention ${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$ and generically
${\rm rk}M_{{\rm id}}=3$, ${\rm rk}W_{0}=2$, i.e. the familiar
$1+2$ finite invariant ${\rm rk}M-aJ=2$, often quoted as rank $3$ for
$M$, the three geometric pieces being the red field, the white canton
and the red emblem.  The $2$–rank above is the exact rank of the
real Greek-cross geometry; the $3$ is the usual rectangular-emblem
idealisation. ∎

4.text:
Write $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{{\rm red}}+b{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}
      =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W,
\tag{1}$$

and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}\,M=1+{\rm rk}\,W$ up to the harmless
translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$.

Put the canton in the $r\times c$ north west block,
$U_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r}$, $V_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$ so that
${\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}=UV^{T}$ is rank one.  Let $H\subset\{1,\dots ,r\}$
and $K\subset\{1,\dots ,c\}$ be the row set of the horizontal arm and
the column set of the vertical arm of the Greek cross in the canton.
A pixel of the canton is red iff $i\in H$ or $j\in K$ and it is white
iff $i\le r,\;j\le c,\;i\notin H,\;j\notin K$.  Hence on the whole
picture

$$W_{ij}=U_{i}V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr)
               \bigl(1-{\bf1}_{K}(j)\bigr)=p_{i}q_{j},$$

with

$$p_{i}=U_{i}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr),\qquad 
q_{j}=V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{K}(j)\bigr),$$

i.e. the white set in the canton is the Cartesian product
$\{i\le r:i\notin H\}\times\{j\le c:j\notin K\}$ the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  In particular

$${\bf1}_{{\rm white}}= (U-H)(V-K)^{T}=pq^{T}$$

is an outer product.  Hence ${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as the canton
contains at least one white row and one white column and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$$

is the sum of the rank-one matrix $aJ$ and the rank-one matrix
$(b-a)pq^{T}$.  Thus

$${\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,$$

and for $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $p\ne0,\;q\ne0$ the
two summands are linearly independent.  Up to the additive constant
$aJ$

$${\rm rk}\,(M-aJ)={\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}M=2, $$

the two independent row types being the all-red rows $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and
the rows $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ inside the canton.  For the
degenerate $a=b$ the matrix is constant, ${\rm rk}M=1$.

In particular the essentially non-trivial white indicator is rank
one.  This is the exact rank of the red field $+$ white canton $-$ Greek
cross.  With the usual textbook rectangular-emblem idealisation
${\bf1}_{{\rm white}}={\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}-{\bf1}_{E}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$
one has ${\rm rk}W\le2$ and

$$M_{{\rm id}}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$$

the sum of three rank-one matrices, ${\rm rk}M_{{\rm id}}\le3$, with
${\rm rk}M_{{\rm id}}=3$ for generic $a\ne b$, i.e. ${\rm rk}W_{{\rm id}}=2$
up to the constant $J$.  The $2$ above is the genuine Greek-cross
rank, the $3$, i.e. $1+2$, being the finite rank of the rectangle-minus-
rectangle idealisation normally quoted in the literature. ∎

11.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$–pixel is
white. Then

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{{\rm red}}+b{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}
      =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,$$

and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$, the translation $M\mapsto
M-aJ$ being inessential.

Put the white canton in the $r\times c$ north west block,
$U_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r },\;V_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$.  Let $H\subset\{1,\dots
,r\}$ and $V\subset\{1,\dots ,c\}$ be the rows and columns occupied by
the horizontal and the vertical arm of the red Greek cross inside the
canton.  A pixel of the canton is white iff it lies in the canton and
it lies in neither arm, i.e.

$$W_{ij}=U_{i}V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr)
                 \bigl(1-{\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr)=p_{i}q_{j},$$

$$p_{i}=U_{i}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr),\qquad 
  q_{j}=V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr),$$

so that on the whole picture $W=pq^{T}$.  The white set is the
Cartesian product

$\{i\le r:i\notin H\}\times\{j\le c:j\notin V\}$

the four corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains a white row and a white
column, and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}.$$

Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,$$

and for $a\ne b$, $p\ne0$, $q\ne0$ the two rank-one summands $J$ and
$pq^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Up to the harmless constant $aJ$
the non-trivial white indicator is rank one; e.g. the three row types
are $a{\bf1}^{T}$ outside the canton, $a{\bf1}^{T}$ on the $H$–rows,
and $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ on the $R_{c}\setminus H$ rows.  Thus
for generic $a\ne b$

$${\rm rk}\,(M-aJ)=1,\qquad {\rm rk}M=2,$$

with the degenerate $a=b$ case ${\rm rk}M=1$.  This is the exact
finite rank of the two-colour Tongan pattern, the red field plus the
rank-one white indicator $pq^{T}$.

Remark.  If the red part of the canton is idealised in the usual
text-book way as a proper axis-parallel rectangle
$E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset uv^{T}$, $W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,
${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$ and

$$M_{id}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$$

is the sum of three rank-one matrices.  In that rectangular-emblem
idealisation ${\rm rk}M_{id}\le3$, and for $0<r_{e}<r,\;0<c_{e}<c$ and
$a\ne b$ the three summands can be made independent, e.g.

$$M_{id}= \begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det M_{id}=-a(b-a)^{2}\ne0,$$

so that the familiar finite geometric invariant quoted for the flag is
${\rm rk}W_{0}=2$, ${\rm rk}M_{id}=3$, i.e. $1+2$ up to the constant
background.  The $2$ above is the rank of the genuine spanning Greek
cross; the $3$ is the rank of the conventional rectangle-minus-rectangle
model. ∎

3.text:
For a two level picture put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{\!T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the
$(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Then with the harmless translation

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{{\rm red}}(i,j)+b{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)
      =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
\end{equation*}
and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$.
Up to the translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the problem is the rank of the
$0\!-\!1$ white indicator.

Put the white canton in the north west $r\times c$ block,
$U_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r},\,V_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$ so that
${\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}=UV^{T}$ is rank one.  On the usual
text-book picture the red emblem which lies in the canton is a proper
axis parallel sub-rectangle

\begin{equation*}
E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T},\qquad 
u_{e,i}={\bf1}_{i_{0}<i\le i_{0}+s},\;\;
v_{e,j}={\bf1}_{j_{0}<j\le j_{0}+t},
\end{equation*}
${\rm rk}E=1$, and on the essential $r\times c$ block

\begin{equation*}
W_{1}={\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}-{\bf1}_{E}=UV^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T} .
\end{equation*}
Hence

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}W_{1}\le {\rm rk}UV^{T}+{\rm rk}u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\le2,
\end{equation*}
and on the whole picture

\begin{equation*}
M=aJ+(b-a)UV^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}
   =a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}
\end{equation*}
is the sum of three rank one matrices.  In particular

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W_{1}\le3,\qquad {\rm rk}W\le2 ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. up to the constant $aJ$ the essential white indicator has
rank $\le2$.  For $0<h_{e}<h$, $0<w_{e}<w$ and $a\ne b$ the three
geometric pieces – the red field $J$, the white canton $UV^{T}$ and the
red emblem $u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ – are linearly independent.  For instance
with $r=c=2$, $r_{e}=c_{e}=1$

\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}
a&b&a\\[2pt] b&b&a\\[2pt] a&a&a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det M=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0,
\]

so that ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for every non-degenerate
$m,n\ge3$ pixelation and $a\ne b$.  Modulo the harmless additive
constant this is the familiar $1+2$ description
${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=2$, ${\rm rk}W=2$, i.e. the three piece red field /
white canton / red rectangle invariant which is quoted in the
literature as the finite geometric rank of the Tongan two-level
picture.  With the constant $J$ counted separately this is the $1+2$
or $4$ statement.

Remark.  With the true Greek cross the horizontal arm spans the whole
width of the canton and the vertical arm spans the whole height of the
canton.  Writing $H_{i}=1$ on the horizontal arm and $W_{j}=1$ on the
vertical arm,

\[
{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)=U_{i}V_{j}(1-H_{i})(1-W_{j})
      =p_{i}q_{j},
\qquad 
p_{i}=U_{i}(1-H_{i}),\;q_{j}=V_{j}(1-W_{j}),
\]

so that $W=pq^{T}$ is exactly rank one.  Then

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
\]

the sum of two rank one matrices, ${\rm rk}M\le2$ and
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$ for $a\ne b$, the $2$-rank being the
exact rank of the real spanning Greek cross.  The $3$-rank above is the
rank of the conventional rectangle-minus-rectangle idealisation of the
emblem, i.e. the finite $1+2$ invariant normally quoted for the flag.
This is the $2$ up to translation which is $3$ with the constant
background counted. ∎

Colleague 10's decomposition already isolates the essential structure: after subtracting the constant background aJ the white indicator on the rectangular-emblem model is exactly the difference of two rank-1 matrices uv^T − u_e v_e^T. Those two outer products, together with J itself, remain linearly independent for generic a ≠ b and any non-degenerate sub-rectangle sizes, which is why the explicit 3-by-3 matrices shown by several colleagues have nonzero determinant and rank exactly 3.  

When the red cross is restored to its true Greek-cross geometry the white set factorizes further into a single outer product pq^T; the rank therefore drops to 2 rather than rising. In either idealization the three geometric pieces (full red field, white canton, red emblem) never generate a fourth independent direction, because the emblem always lies strictly inside the canton and the overlap term that would appear from splitting the cross is already absorbed by the subtraction that defines the white indicator. Consequently adjoining extra rows or columns outside the canton merely repeats the constant row a·1^T and cannot increase the rank. The attainable maximum therefore stays at 3 for every finite pixelation, matching the consensus already reached by colleagues 3, 8, 12 and 13.
public_text.7: Colleague 10's explicit 3-by-3 matrix already attains rank exactly 3 for generic a ≠ b, and the same three linearly independent row patterns recur at every finite resolution: the constant-a rows outside the canton, the mixed rows that intersect only the white canton rectangle, and the rows that further intersect the inner red emblem. Those three patterns span the entire row space once the constant background J is included, so the decomposition M = aJ + (b-a)uv^T - (b-a)u_e v_e^T is already maximal. Treating the red cross as separate horizontal and vertical slabs cannot add a fourth direction; the two slab indicators are linear combinations of the canton indicator and the single emblem correction already present, exactly as colleagues 1, 5 and 7 observed. Hence the attainable rank remains capped at 3 under the rectangular-emblem model that matches every published finite-pixel analysis of the Tongan flag. Refining the grid or invoking a genuine curved emblem merely pushes the rank toward the continuum supremum min(m,n), which is irrelevant to the finite-pixel question posed.

Colleague 10's decomposition already gives the cleanest accounting: after translating by the constant background aJ, the white indicator on the canton block is exactly uv^T − u_e v_e^T. These two outer products are linearly independent whenever the emblem rectangle is a proper sub-rectangle of the canton (0 < r_e < r, 0 < c_e < c), and adjoining the constant term therefore yields a three-dimensional span. The explicit 3-by-3 matrices posted earlier attain det M = −a(b−a)^2 ≠ 0, confirming that the three row patterns—one constant-a outside the canton, one b-filled on the canton interior, and one mixed on the emblem—are independent for generic a ≠ b.  

Any attempt to split the red cross into separate horizontal and vertical rank-1 slabs immediately collapses: the center square where the arms intersect is counted twice, so the two slab indicators differ from the single rectangular emblem correction by a rank-1 adjustment that already lies inside the span of uv^T and u_e v_e^T. Consequently the four nominal terms reduce to the same three independent matrices already identified, and no fourth direction appears. Refining the pixel grid outside the canton merely repeats the constant row a·1^T, which cannot increase the rank. The attainable maximum therefore remains exactly 3 on every finite rectangular pixelation.
public_text.14: Colleague 10's phrasing that the bound is "1+2 or 4 with the all-ones term counted separately" is the exact point that needs clarification. When we expand M = aJ + (b-a)uv^T - (b-a)u^e v^e^T, the three rank-1 matrices are already the complete generating set; adjoining any fourth candidate vector (for instance an extra indicator for one arm of the cross) immediately produces a linear dependence because that arm lies inside the canton rectangle already spanned by uv^T. The explicit 3-by-3 matrices posted by colleagues 3, 8 and 12 have nonzero determinant, confirming that these three directions are independent for generic a ≠ b and that the row space cannot be enlarged by further rows or columns outside the canton. Hence the attainable maximum remains exactly 3; any apparent fourth dimension is absorbed by the dependence that holds uniformly for every rectangular pixelation. I would be interested to hear from colleagues 10 and 2 whether they see a concrete construction that escapes this dependence and actually realises rank 4, or whether the "4" label is merely an informal overcount that collapses once the geometry is written out.

Colleague 10 and several others have already laid out the clean decomposition M = aJ + (b-a)(uv^T - u_e v_e^T) under the rectangular-emblem model that the literature conventionally adopts for finite pixelations; the three rank-1 terms remain linearly independent for generic a ≠ b, as confirmed by the shared 3-by-3 determinant examples.  

Even if one instead decomposes the red cross inside the canton into separate horizontal and vertical slabs (each an outer product), the overlap square is itself rank-1 and produces an immediate linear dependence that collapses the four nominal indicators back into the same three-dimensional span already generated by the constant background, the full canton rectangle, and the single emblem correction. Consequently no fourth independent direction appears, the row space stays at most three-dimensional, and the attainable rank remains exactly 3 on any non-degenerate rectangular pixelation. Refining the grid outside the canton merely repeats the constant row a·1^T and cannot increase the count. This is consistent with the explicit matrices already posted and with the finite geometric invariant quoted for the flag.

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and put
$W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Then on any raster

$$
M_{ij}=a{\bf 1}_{{\rm red}}+b{\bf 1}_{{\rm white}}
      =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$.  Up to the harmless translation
$M\mapsto M-aJ$ the problem is the rank of the white indicator.

Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the row and column sets which meet the white
canton and let $R_{h}\subset R_{c}$, $C_{v}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows
and columns occupied by the horizontal and the vertical arm of the red
Greek cross in the canton.  A pixel of the canton is white iff its row
is in $R_{c}\setminus R_{h}$ and its column is in $C_{c}\setminus C_{v}$.
Hence with

$$
p_{i}={\bf1}_{R_{c}\setminus R_{h}}(i),\qquad
q_{j}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus C_{v}}(j)
$$

$$
W_{ij}=U_{i}V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{R_{h}}(i)\bigr)
          \bigl(1-{\bf1}_{C_{v}}(j)\bigr)=p_{i}q_{j},
$$

i.e. on the $r\times c$ canton

$$
W_{1}=(U-H)(V-V_{0})^{T}=p q^{T},
$$

the four corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains at least one white row and
one white column and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
$$

the sum of the rank-one matrix $aJ$ and the rank-one matrix
$(b-a)pq^{T}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $p\ne0,q\ne0$ the two
summands are linearly independent.  Up to the constant background
${\rm rk}(M-aJ)={\rm rk}W=1$ is the essentially non-trivial rank, the
two independent row types being the all-red rows $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and the
rows $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ inside the canton.  With the
degeneracy $a=b$ the matrix is constant of rank $1$, $0$ after the
translation.

Remark.  This is the exact Greek-cross geometry.  If the red emblem
in the canton is idealised as a proper axis-parallel rectangle
$E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset uv^{T}$ then
$W_{{\rm id}}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ has ${\rm rk}W_{{\rm id}}\le2$ and

$$
M_{{\rm id}}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}
$$

is the familiar sum of three rank-one matrices, ${\rm rk}M_{{\rm id}}
\le3$, generically ${\rm rk}M_{{\rm id}}=3$, ${\rm rk}W_{{\rm id}}=2$.
The $1+2$ or $3$-rank is the finite invariant normally quoted for the
rectangle-minus-rectangle idealisation of the Tongan pattern; it
collapses to the $1+1$ or $2$-rank $M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$ for the real
spanning Greek cross. ∎

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.
Then

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad 
{\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W ,
$$

so up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the rank is the rank
of the white indicator.  Put the canton in the first $r$ rows and the
first $c$ columns, $u_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$,
${\bf1}_{C}=uv^{T}$ rank one.  In the usual finite–resolution
text–book idealisation the red part of the canton is a proper
axis–parallel sub–rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset {\bf1}_{C}$,
${\rm rk}E=1$, so that on the essential $r\times c$ block

$$
W_{1}={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T},\qquad 
{\rm rk}\,W_{1}\le2,
$$

and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}
$$

is the sum of three rank–one matrices.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}uv^{T}+{\rm rk}u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\le3,
\qquad {\rm rk}W\le2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$, $0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$ the three matrices
$J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  E.g. with
$r=c=2$, $r_{e}=c_{e}=1$

$$
M=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det M=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for every non–degenerate $m\ge3,\,
n\ge3$ pixelation and $a\ne b$.  Up to the constant background
$M-aJ$ has the two independent pieces $uv^{T}$ and $u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,
i.e. ${\rm rk}W=2$, ${\rm rk}M-aJ=2$, the familiar $1+2$ finite
geometric invariant, often quoted as rank $3$ for $M$ and rank $2$ for
the white indicator.

Remark.  With the exact spanning Greek cross the red part of the
canton is $H V^{T}+U W^{T}-HW^{T}$ and

$$
W_{{\rm white}}=UV^{T}-HV^{T}-UW^{T}+HW^{T}
       =(U-H)(V-W)^{T}=p q^{T},
$$

so that $W$ is an outer product, ${\rm rk}W=1$ and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}
$$

has ${\rm rk}M\le2$ with ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\ne b$ and
${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$.  This is the $p q^{T}$ factorisation of the four
corner white rectangles of the genuine flag.  The $3$ above is the
finite rank of the red–field/white–canton/red–rectangle model which
collapses to the $2$, i.e. $1$ up to translation, rank of the exact
spanning cross.  In the continuum limit the $0\!-\!1$ indicator ceases
to be finite rank and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M=\min\{m,n\}$. ∎

On a raster let $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel
$(i,j)$ is white.  Then

$$
M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{{\rm red}}+b{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}
     =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W ,
\tag{1}
$$

and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ up to the harmless translation
$M\mapsto M-aJ$.

Let the white canton be the $r\times c$ north west block,
$U_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r}$, $V_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$.  Let $H\subset\{1,\dots ,r\}$
and $K\subset\{1,\dots ,c\}$ be the row- and column-sets occupied by the
horizontal and the vertical arm of the Greek cross in the canton.  A
pixel of the canton is white iff its row is in the canton and it is not
in $H$ and its column is in the canton and it is not in $K$.  Hence

$$
{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)=U_{i}V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr)
               \bigl(1-{\bf1}_{K}(j)\bigr)=p_{i}q_{j},
$$

with

$$
p_{i}=U_{i}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr),\qquad 
q_{j}=V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{K}(j)\bigr),
$$

so that on the whole picture

$$
W=pq^{T}
$$

is an outer product.  The white set is the Cartesian product
$\{i\le r:i\notin H\}\times\{j\le c:j\notin K\}$, i.e. the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}\,W=1$ as soon as the
canton contains at least one white row and one white column and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}
$$

is the sum of the rank-one matrix $aJ$ and the rank-one matrix
$(b-a)pq^{T}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $p\ne0,\;q\ne0$ the two
summands are linearly independent.  Up to the constant background
$M-aJ$ the essentially non-trivial part is rank one,

$$
{\rm rk}\,(M-aJ)={\rm rk}W=1,\qquad 
{\rm rk}M=2\;\;a\ne b,
$$

the two independent row types being the all-red rows $a{\bf1}^{T}$ and
the rows $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ inside the canton.  The
degenerate case $a=b$ gives the constant matrix ${\rm rk}M=1$.  This is
the exact finite geometric rank of the real Tongan red field $+$ white
canton $-$ Greek cross.

Remark.  The often quoted $1+2$ bound
${\rm rk}M\le3,\;{\rm rk}W\le2$ is the rank of the textbook
rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,
$M_{0}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$, i.e. the red field, the white
canton rectangle and a proper sub-rectangle emblem.  In that
idealisation ${\rm rk}M_{0}\le3$ and ${\rm rk}M_{0}=3$ for generic
$a\ne b$, e.g.

$$
M_{0}=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a
\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det M_{0}=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0,
$$

so that ${\rm rk}W_{0}=2$ up to translation.  The $3$-rank is the finite
invariant of the red-field/white-canton/red-rectangle model; the Greek
cross factorises the white set to $pq^{T}$ and reduces the genuine
finite geometric rank to the $2$, i.e. $1$ up to the constant
background, quoted above.  In the continuum limit the $0\!-\!1$
indicator ceases to be finite rank and the supremum over refinements is
$\min(m,n)$. ∎

On a raster put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff $(i,j)$ is white.
Then with two levels

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le1+{\rm rk}\,W,
$$

and for $a\ne b$, ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$ up to the harmless
translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$.

Let ${\mathcal R}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$ and ${\mathcal C}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$
be the rows and columns which meet the white canton and let
$H\subset{\mathcal R}$ and $V\subset{\mathcal C}$ be the rows and columns
of the horizontal and the vertical arm of the Greek cross.  Inside the
canton a pixel is red iff $i\in H$ or $j\in V$ and it is white iff
$i\in{\mathcal R}\setminus H$ and $j\in{\mathcal C}\setminus V$.  Hence on the
whole picture

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{{\mathcal R}}(i){\bf1}_{{\mathcal C}}(j)
       \bigl[1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr]\bigl[1-{\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr]
     =p_{i}q_{j},
$$

with

$$
p_{i}={\bf1}_{{\mathcal R}\setminus H}(i),\qquad 
q_{j}={\bf1}_{{\mathcal C}\setminus V}(j),
$$

i.e. on the $r\times c$ canton

$$
W_{1}=( {\bf1}_{r}-h)( {\bf1}_{c}-v)^{T},
$$

$h={\bf1}_{H}$, $v={\bf1}_{V}$.  The white set is the Cartesian product
${\mathcal R}\setminus H\times{\mathcal C}\setminus V$ – the four corner
rectangles of the canton – so $W=pq^{T}$ is an outer product.  In
particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains at least one white row
and one white column, and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
$$

is the sum of the rank-one matrix $aJ$ and the rank-one matrix
$(b-a)pq^{T}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $p\ne0,\;q\ne0$ the
two summands are linearly independent.  With the harmless
normalisation $M-aJ$ the essentially non-trivial part is
${\rm rk}(M-aJ)={\rm rk}W=1$; with the constant background counted
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate $a=b$ case.

The $1+2$ bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$,

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T},
$$

is the rank of the usual rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$.  In that idealisation the three
matrices $J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are generically independent and the
familiar finite invariant is ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W_{0}=2$, i.e.
$1+2$ up to translation.  For the genuine spanning Greek cross the
red part of the canton factorises and the white indicator is the rank
one product $pq^{T}$ above, so the exact finite geometric rank of the
two-level Tongan pattern is the $2$ above, $1$ up to the constant

rectangular-emblem idealisation.

Write $J={\bf 1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$–pixel is
white. Then

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{{\rm red}}+b{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}
      =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,$$

and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$, the translation $M\mapsto
M-aJ$ being inessential.

Put the white canton in the $r\times c$ north west block,
$U_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r },\;V_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$.  Let $H\subset\{1,\dots
,r\}$ and $V\subset\{1,\dots ,c\}$ be the rows and columns occupied by
the horizontal and the vertical arm of the red Greek cross inside the
canton.  A pixel of the canton is white iff it lies in the canton and
it lies in neither arm, i.e.

$$W_{ij}=U_{i}V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr)
                 \bigl(1-{\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr)=p_{i}q_{j},$$

$$p_{i}=U_{i}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{H}(i)\bigr),\qquad 
  q_{j}=V_{j}\bigl(1-{\bf1}_{V}(j)\bigr),$$

so that on the whole picture $W=pq^{T}$.  The white set is the
Cartesian product

$\{i\le r:i\notin H\}\times\{j\le c:j\notin V\}$

the four corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains a white row and a white
column, and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}.$$

Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=2,$$

and for $a\ne b$, $p\ne0$, $q\ne0$ the two rank-one summands $J$ and
$pq^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Up to the harmless constant $aJ$
the non-trivial white indicator is rank one; e.g. the three row types
are $a{\bf1}^{T}$ outside the canton, $a{\bf1}^{T}$ on the $H$–rows,
and $a{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)p_{i}q^{T}$ on the $R_{c}\setminus H$ rows.  Thus
for generic $a\ne b$

$${\rm rk}\,(M-aJ)=1,\qquad {\rm rk}M=2,$$

with the degenerate $a=b$ case ${\rm rk}M=1$.  This is the exact
finite rank of the two-colour Tongan pattern, the red field plus the
rank-one white indicator $pq^{T}$.

Remark.  If the red part of the canton is idealised in the usual
text-book way as a proper axis-parallel rectangle
$E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset uv^{T}$, $W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,
${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$ and

$$M_{id}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$$

is the sum of three rank-one matrices.  In that rectangular-emblem
idealisation ${\rm rk}M_{id}\le3$, and for $0<r_{e}<r,\;0<c_{e}<c$ and
$a\ne b$ the three summands can be made independent, e.g.

$$M_{id}= \begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det M_{id}=-a(b-a)^{2}\ne0,$$

so that the familiar finite geometric invariant quoted for the flag is
${\rm rk}W_{0}=2$, ${\rm rk}M_{id}=3$, i.e. $1+2$ up to the constant
background.  The $2$ above is the rank of the genuine spanning Greek
cross; the $3$ is the rank of the conventional rectangle-minus-rectangle
model. ∎
public_text.3:
For a two level picture put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{\!T}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the
$(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Then with the harmless translation

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{{\rm red}}(i,j)+b{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)
      =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
\end{equation*}
and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$.
Up to the translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the problem is the rank of the
$0\!-\!1$ white indicator.

Put the white canton in the north west $r\times c$ block,
$U_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r},\,V_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$ so that
${\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}=UV^{T}$ is rank one.  On the usual
text-book picture the red emblem which lies in the canton is a proper
axis parallel sub-rectangle

\begin{equation*}
E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T},\qquad 
u_{e,i}={\bf1}_{i_{0}<i\le i_{0}+s},\;\;
v_{e,j}={\bf1}_{j_{0}<j\le j_{0}+t},
\end{equation*}
${\rm rk}E=1$, and on the essential $r\times c$ block

\begin{equation*}
W_{1}={\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}-{\bf1}_{E}=UV^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T} .
\end{equation*}
Hence

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}W_{1}\le {\rm rk}UV^{T}+{\rm rk}u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\le2,
\end{equation*}
and on the whole picture

\begin{equation*}
M=aJ+(b-a)UV^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}
   =a{\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}
\end{equation*}
is the sum of three rank one matrices.  In particular

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W_{1}\le3,\qquad {\rm rk}W\le2 ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. up to the constant $aJ$ the essential white indicator has
rank $\le2$.  For $0<h_{e}<h$, $0<w_{e}<w$ and $a\ne b$ the three
geometric pieces – the red field $J$, the white canton $UV^{T}$ and the
red emblem $u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ – are linearly independent.  For instance
with $r=c=2$, $r_{e}=c_{e}=1$

\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}
a&b&a\\[2pt] b&b&a\\[2pt] a&a&a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det M=-(a-b)^{2}a\ne0,
\]

so that ${\rm rk}M=3$ is attained for every non-degenerate
$m,n\ge3$ pixelation and $a\ne b$.  Modulo the harmless additive
constant this is the familiar $1+2$ description
${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=2$, ${\rm rk}W=2$, i.e. the three piece red field /
white canton / red rectangle invariant which is quoted in the
literature as the finite geometric rank of the Tongan two-level
picture.  With the constant $J$ counted separately this is the $1+2$
or $4$ statement.

Remark.  With the true Greek cross the horizontal arm spans the whole
width of the canton and the vertical arm spans the whole height of the
canton.  Writing $H_{i}=1$ on the horizontal arm and $W_{j}=1$ on the
vertical arm,

\[
{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)=U_{i}V_{j}(1-H_{i})(1-W_{j})
      =p_{i}q_{j},
\qquad 
p_{i}=U_{i}(1-H_{i}),\;q_{j}=V_{j}(1-W_{j}),
\]

so that $W=pq^{T}$ is exactly rank one.  Then

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T},
\]

the sum of two rank one matrices, ${\rm rk}M\le2$ and
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$ for $a\ne b$, the $2$-rank being the
exact rank of the real spanning Greek cross.  The $3$-rank above is the
rank of the conventional rectangle-minus-rectangle idealisation of the
emblem, i.e. the finite $1+2$ invariant normally quoted for the flag.
This is the $2$ up to translation which is $3$ with the constant
background counted. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-valued picture can be written $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$ and for $a\ne b$ ${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$.

Exact Greek-cross geometry. Let $R_{c},C_{c}$ be the rows/columns meeting the canton and $R_{h}\subset R_{c}$, $C_{v}\subset C_{c}$ the rows/columns of the horizontal and vertical arm. A pixel is white in the canton iff its row is in $R_{c}\setminus R_{h}$ and its column is in $C_{c}\setminus C_{v}$. Hence

$W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{R_{c}}(i){\bf1}_{C_{c}}(j)[1-{\bf1}_{R_{h}}(i)][1-{\bf1}_{C_{v}}(j)]
      =p_{i}q_{j}$,

$p=U-H,\;q=V-V_{c}$, $W=pq^{T}$. The white set is the Cartesian product $(R_{c}\!\setminus\!R_{h})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!C_{v})$, i.e. the four corner rectangles of the canton. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as the canton contains a white row and a white column and

$M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices. For $a\ne b$, $p\ne0$, $q\ne0$, $J$ and $pq^{T}$ are independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}(M-aJ)=1$. The $a=b$ degenerate case is the constant matrix of rank $1$, $0$ after translation. This is the $1+1$ exact count $M=aJ+(b-a)pq^{T}$ put forward by colleagues 4,10,11,12,2,4,8.

Rectangular-emblem idealisation. If the red part of the canton is idealised as a proper axis-parallel sub-rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset uv^{T}$ with $W_{0}=uv^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$, then

$M_{id}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}-(b-a)u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$

is a sum of three rank-one matrices, ${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$, ${\rm rk}M_{id}\le3$. For $0<r_{e}<r$, $0<c_{e}<c$ and $a\ne b$ the three matrices $J,uv^{T},u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are generically independent, e.g.

$\begin{pmatrix}a&b&a\\ b&b&a\\ a&a&a\end{pmatrix}$ with $\det=-a(b-a)^{2}\ne0$,

so ${\rm rk}M_{id}=3$, ${\rm rk}W_{0}=2$, the familiar $1+2$ finite invariant quoted by colleagues 1,3,8,10,11,13,14. This is the three-piece red field / white canton / red rectangle model.

Disagreement and status. Round 2 shows a split: colleagues 10,11,12,2,4,8 give the exact factorisation $W=pq^{T}$ and rank $2$, $1$ up to constant, noting that the rectangular-emblem $3$ is an idealisation. Colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 continue to defend the rectangular-emblem $3$-rank as the attainable finite-pixel maximum, with the explicit $3\times3$ determinant as evidence.
